newsitem.title: FRANCE: Northwest signs for 50 Airbus jets.
newsitem.headline: Northwest signs for 50 Airbus jets.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp. has committed to buy 50 A319 jets from Airbus Industrie and take options on up to 100 more in an agreement worth at least $2 billion, the European aircraft consortium announced Thursday.
The agreement signed by the Eagan, Minn.-based airline is a commitment to buy rather than a firm order.

The value of the 50 aircraft is estimated at about $2 billion, based on an average price of around $40 million for an A319. Airbus said delivery of the 125-seat, twin-engine jets is scheduled for 1999 through 2003.
"We are hopeful that this memorandum of understanding will result in a final agreement in the near future," Airbus quoted Northwest Chief Executive John Dasburg as saying.
The A319 is a smaller version of the A320 and A321. All three aircraft feature identical flight decks and the widest passenger cabins of any single-aisle aircraft, Airbus said.
Northwest currently operates 50 A320s and has a previously announced contract for 20 A320s to be delivered in 1998 and 1999.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Germany's Daimler-Benz AG; and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA of Spain.
It is the world's No. 2 aircraft maker after Seattle-based Boeing Co.
